This applies to xslt_transform, sign, verify_signature, create_certificate, schema_analysis, xsd_generate, sample_generate, spreadsheet_convert, format (meta.mode = format or minify), schematron_check, quick_fix (a fix that does not apply to the document is invalid_input, a skipped one cancelled with meta.reason), replace (meta.kind = xpath/text, meta.scope = document/files), file_search (meta.kind, files searched and files that could not be read), debug_run (meta.language = xslt/xquery/schematron, meta.stage = start/run, a stopped run is cancelled), xsd_flatten, type_usages, schema_library (meta.action), template_insert and update_apply. A dialog that belongs to such an action is not counted a second time.

A PDF generation (fop_pdf) names the stage that ran last in meta.stage (transform = the XSLT run that produces the XSL-FO, render = Apache FOP rendering it) and, for a failure, the processor's error code or the exception class in error_code. A stylesheet that does not compile or an XSL-FO document FOP rejects (ValidationException) is a problem with the user's files and has status invalid_input; the error dialog of such a run is not reported a second time. A schema documentation run (schema_doc) records the format (meta.format), the duration and, for a failure, the exception class in error_code; a schema that does not parse (SAXParseException) has status invalid_input.

The spreadsheet converter (spreadsheet_convert) records the direction in meta.direction (to_spreadsheet or to_xml), the format in meta.format (xlsx, xls or csv), the duration, the size of the exported document in characters (input_bytes) and, for a failure, the exception class in error_code. A document that is not well-formed has status invalid_input; one with more rows than a sheet holds, or too large for the memory limit, has status unsupported.

Identical errors are sent only once per session (with a repeat counter), and at most 30 error events are sent per session.

docs.title: Launch, session and performance information
docs.text: Event What it contains app_start Startup time in ms, is_first_run, meta.channel (release or dev), meta.days_since_install (whole days since the anonymous ID was created), meta.package (installer, portable or none — only the kind of installation, never its folder), meta.install_source (distribution channel: standalone for a direct download, winget, scoop, homebrew or flatpak; a winget install is recognised from the second start on) and a snapshot of a few UI settings (meta.set_theme, set_toolbar_labels, set_toolbar_icons, set_activity_labels, set_rendering, set_update_check, set_xml_autoformat, set_xsd_autosave, set_schema_autobind — on/off values and fixed options only). app_exit Session length, number of opened files, actions, side panels and the maximum number of open tabs, plus the peak (sampled while the app runs) and maximum Java heap rounded to 64 MB. prev_session_crashed Sent at the next start when the previous session ended without a clean exit (crash, forced close). Contains only that session's anonymous ID and app version. The detection uses small marker files in ~/.freeXmlToolkit/sessions/. If the Java runtime itself crashed, it leaves a crash file (hs_err_pid<pid>.log) behind; the app then adds meta.jvm_crash with three fixed pieces read from that file's header: the signal (crash_signal, e.g. EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION), the faulting library or Java method (crash_frame, e.g. C fontmanager.dll) and the thread name (crash_thread). Paths, addresses, registers and the rest of the file are never read or sent, and the file is left in place. file_open, view_mode, validate, schema_analysis, schema_bind How long opening a document, switching to the Text/Tree/Graphic view, validating or analyzing took, and the document size. schema_bind tells how a schema was found for an opened document (declared, library, catalog, manual or none); when a referenced schema could not be bound, it names the source that was tried and the reason in meta.failure (unresolved = the reference could not be resolved or reached, unloadable = the schema was found but could not be loaded) and the form of the reference in meta.ref_kind (http, file, relative, urn or other) — never the location itself. A relative or file reference that cannot be resolved names a local file that does not exist (next to the document, or at an absolute path, e.g. one written on another machine) and is sent with status invalid_input. A file that cannot be read is recorded as file_open with status invalid_input (missing, unreadable or not decodable: the exception class in error_code) or error (an app failure, with its stack signature); a file that cannot be written is file_save with the same classification. An opened file and a failed write carry the name of the document's character encoding in meta.charset when it is not UTF-8 (for example windows-1252). A validation that could not run — the schema or Schematron does not load, or the validator itself failed — is validate with status invalid_input or error and the error code; problems in the document are error_count on a status ok event. A file that is not opened because of its size is recorded as file_open with status cancelled (the user declined the large-file warning) or unsupported (it does not fit into the memory limit), its size, meta.reason=too_large and the memory limit (meta.heap_max_mb). ui_stall The user interface did not respond for at least two seconds: the duration, the side panel and view mode that were active, a stack signature of the blocked code (code locations only, as for errors), and the shape of the active document: its size in characters (input_bytes), its number of lines (meta.lines) and the length class of its longest line (meta.max_line_len: <1k, <10k, <100k, >=100k; unknown above 50,000 lines, which are not scanned) — never its content. Also the garbage-collection time during the block in ms (meta.gc_ms), the heap usage at its end in percent of the memory limit (meta.heap_pct) and meta.cause=gc when collections took at least half of the block (the memory was nearly full). Pauses of the whole application (system sleep) and waits in the operating system's own loops (window dragging or live resizing, native file dialogs, showing a native popup window) are not reported. At most 10 per session. ui_freeze The user interface has not responded for ten seconds and is still blocked. Sent right away, while the freeze lasts, so that a freeze ending in a forced close is not lost: the time blocked so far, the side panel, view mode and document type, a stack signature of the blocked code (code locations only), and the memory load (meta.gc_ms, meta.heap_pct, meta.cause=gc) as for ui_stall. The document shape is not included. If the interface recovers, the regular ui_stall follows. At most 3 per session. ui_command, panel_action Which toolbar button, keyboard shortcut (e.g. mod+s), Welcome page card or side-panel action was used (fixed identifiers). edit_summary Counts per session of editing commands in the structured editors (e.g. add_element: 12, undo: 3) and of IntelliSense suggestions shown/accepted — command names only, never element names, values or text.

docs.title: What is never collected
docs.text:
• File names, folder names or paths
  • Document content, XPath/XQuery expressions, schema or element names
  • Exception messages (they often contain paths or content — only class names and code locations are used)
  • User names, e-mail addresses, the "User Info" from the settings, license or machine identifiers
  • Your IP address: the server derives only the country from it and never stores or logs the IP

docs.title: Error reports you send yourself
docs.text: Error dialogs, the About dialog and the Help menu offer Send error report… / Report a problem…. There you describe the problem in your own words and may optionally leave a contact address if you would like a reply. The checkbox Include technical details attaches the exception class, fingerprint and stack signature described above. A collapsible Preview shows exactly the JSON that will be sent.

docs.title: How to see what is sent
docs.text: Settings → Privacy → USAGE STATISTICS → What is sent? shows a sample of the exact payload (built from the events currently waiting to be sent) together with your anonymous installation ID.

docs.title: How to switch it off
docs.text:
Open Settings → Privacy → USAGE STATISTICS and clear

  • Send anonymous usage statistics and/or
  • Send anonymous error reports,

then click Save Settings. Events of the disabled kind that are still waiting to be sent are deleted immediately.

Administrators can disable telemetry completely by starting the application with the Java system property -Dfxt.telemetry.disabled=true, or by setting these keys in ~/.freeXmlToolkit/FreeXmlToolkit.properties:

telemetry.usage.enabled=false
telemetry.errors.enabled=false

docs.title: How to reset the installation ID
docs.text: Settings → Privacy → USAGE STATISTICS → What is sent? → Reset ID replaces the anonymous installation ID with a new random one. Data sent afterwards can no longer be linked to data sent before.

docs.title: Where the data goes
docs.text: Events are sent over HTTPS to https://telemetry.status20.net, a self-hosted server operated by the FreeXmlToolkit author in the EU (Helsinki, Finland). The data is not shared with third parties and is used only to understand which features are used and which errors occur. Individual events are deleted automatically after 90 days; long-term, only anonymous, aggregated daily totals (counts per feature, version and operating system) are kept. Error reports you send yourself via Send error report… are kept until they have been reviewed. The country is derived from your IP address using the free DB-IP country database (IP Geolocation by DB-IP, CC BY 4.0); the IP address itself is never stored or logged.

docs.title: Offline use and proxies
docs.text: Events are queued locally in ~/.freeXmlToolkit/telemetry-queue.jsonl (at most 5000 events and 14 days, oldest dropped first) and sent in small batches about every five minutes. Requests use the proxy configured in Settings → Network & Security → HTTP PROXY. If the server cannot be reached, sending is retried later with increasing pauses (up to six hours); the application is never slowed down.

docs.title: Template Management
docs.text:
Reusable XML snippets and document skeletons: insert them into the document you are editing, or start a new file from one. Templates can carry ${parameter} placeholders that you fill in when the template is used.

Templates power the New File dialog

Templates also appear in the guided New File dialog (filtered to the matching file type), so a brand-new document can start from a template instead of a blank page. You manage your own templates in the Settings → Editor → TEMPLATES card. See Creating templates for the New File dialog.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Templates in the Unified Shell: the Insert Template dialog and the TEMPLATES settings card

Templates let you keep document structures you type again and again - a SOAP envelope, a Maven POM, a CDATA section, a Schematron rule - and drop them into the editor with a few clicks. The parts written as ${name} are parameters: when you use a template that has parameters, FreeXmlToolkit asks for their values first and then inserts the finished text.

There are two places where templates are used:

Where What it does Insert Template (Edit → Insert Template… or Ctrl+T) Inserts a template at the caret of the active document New File dialog (toolbar New or Ctrl+N) Creates a new document from a template of the selected file type

docs.title: Inserting a Template
docs.text:
1. Open (or create) the document you want to edit and place the caret where the snippet should go.
  2. Press Ctrl+T or choose Edit → Insert Template… in the menu bar.
  3. The Insert Template dialog lists all templates as name — category; select one to see its content in the Preview box. OK is enabled once a template is selected.
  4. If the template has parameters, a second dialog asks for each value (defaults are pre-filled where the template defines them). Cancelling this dialog inserts nothing.
  5. The rendered text is inserted at the caret. Undo (Ctrl+Z) removes it again in one step.

The dialog is only available while a document is open; with no active document the shortcut does nothing.

docs.title: Built-in Templates
docs.text:
FreeXmlToolkit ships with a set of ready-made templates, grouped by category, for example:

Category Examples Basic simple-element, element-with-attributes, cdata-section, xml-comment Web services soap-envelope, rest-response, wsdl-service Build & configuration spring-config, maven-pom, api-documentation Industry financial-transaction, patient-record, vehicle-information, government-form Schema xsd-schema

Built-in templates cannot be edited, but you can create your own with the same content and change it freely.

docs.title: Managing Your Own Templates
docs.text: Your templates are managed in Settings (gear icon at the bottom of the activity bar), in the TEMPLATES card (group Editor in the Settings side panel). Template changes are saved right away - you do not need to click Save Settings.

docs.title: Set the templates folder
docs.text:
1. In the TEMPLATES card, use Browse… next to Templates directory to choose the folder where your templates are kept (leave it empty for the default location, ~/.freeXmlToolkit/templates, or the bundled examples/templates folder when it exists).
  2. The change takes effect right away - no restart needed.

docs.title: Add or change a template
docs.text:
Below the folder you find the list Your templates with three buttons:

Button Action New Opens the New Template dialog. Fill in Name, Category, Description, File type and Content. Edit Opens the selected template in the Edit Template dialog to change any of its fields. Delete Removes the selected template.

Each template is saved as a .template file in the templates folder, so you can copy those files to another machine or share them with colleagues. The File type you pick decides where the template shows up in the New File dialog: it appears only when that same file type is selected.

docs.title: Creating templates for the New File dialog
docs.text:
1. Click New on the toolbar (Ctrl+N), or New file in the Explorer panel.
  2. Choose the File type that matches your template.
  3. Open the Template list - your templates appear alongside the built-in ones.
  4. Select it; if it has parameters, you are prompted to fill them in.
  5. Optionally choose a Save to location, then confirm to create the document.

See New File dialog for the other options of that dialog.

docs.title: Placeholders and Parameters
docs.text:
Write placeholders as ${name} anywhere in the template content:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<${rootElement}>
    <header>
        <title>${documentTitle}</title>
        <version>${version}</version>
    </header>
</${rootElement}>

When the template is used, every ${name} is replaced by the value you enter. A placeholder can be used several times (${rootElement} above appears twice and is filled in once).

Templates created with the built-in library or programmatically can declare typed parameters (string, integer, decimal, boolean, date, email, URL, or a list of allowed values); the parameter dialog validates the input accordingly and offers default values where defined.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+T Insert Template into the active document Ctrl+N New File dialog (choose a template there)

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: Tip Description Keep it simple Smaller templates are more reusable Clear names Use descriptive parameter names such as ${customerId} instead of ${x} Use categories The Insert Template dialog shows name — category, so consistent categories make long lists scannable One file type per template Pick the File type carefully - it controls where the template is offered in the New File dialog

docs.title: Transform Panel
docs.text:
The panel is organized into collapsible sections (STYLESHEET, INPUT, OUTPUT METHOD, PARAMETERS) with a single primary Run Transform button and a Run automatically checkbox next to it. Results do not open as an editor tab - they appear in the OUTPUT panel docked below the editor. The run options (checkboxes) and the advanced tools share the OPTIONS & TOOLS section at the top of the panel.

The Transform panel (open it from the Transform icon in the activity bar on the left) runs XSLT transformations. XPath, XQuery and JSONPath queries against the open document live in the Query Console - the panel shows a short hint with an Open Query Console button for them. The panel header reads TRANSFORM; the run options and tools are in the OPTIONS & TOOLS section (see OPTIONS & TOOLS below). Each section header is clickable to collapse or expand that section.

Tip

For a quick transform without opening this panel, right-click XML files in the Explorer and choose Transform with …. It shares the same recent-stylesheet list and shows its result in the same OUTPUT panel.

docs.title: STYLESHEET
docs.text:
• Shows the name of the chosen XSLT stylesheet on its own line below the icon, the favorites/browse controls and Change (long names are shortened in the middle; hover for the full path). While no stylesheet is set, the row reads "No stylesheet — choose or drop a file" - clicking it works like Change.
  • Change - pick an .xsl / .xslt file from disk (it is also loaded into the editor).
  • The clock icon opens the recent stylesheets menu: reapply a recently used stylesheet in a single click (it is also loaded into the editor), or choose Clear recent to empty the list.
  • The star icon opens your XSLT favorites - see Browsing favorites with ◀ / ▶ below. A picked stylesheet is also loaded into the editor.
  • Drag & drop: drop an .xsl / .xslt file from your file manager straight onto the STYLESHEET row - it becomes the current stylesheet and is loaded into the editor, exactly as if you had picked it from a favorite. While dragging, the row glows green when the file can be loaded and red when it has the wrong extension (a red drop is rejected). As with favorites, the transform runs automatically as soon as both a stylesheet and an input are ready (while Run automatically is checked).

docs.title: INPUT
docs.text:
The INPUT section shows which document the transform will use as its input (the name on its own line, the full path as tooltip; "No input — open a document or drop a file" while there is none):

  • By default the input follows the active editor document: switch to another tab and the next run transforms that document (the shown input name updates live).
  • Change opens a small menu with two options:
    • Select XML file… - transform a fixed XML file from disk instead, regardless of which editor tab is active.
    • Use active editor - go back to following the active tab.
  • The star icon opens your XML favorites - see Browsing favorites with ◀ / ▶ below. A picked input is also opened in the editor and becomes the active tab.
  • Drag & drop: drop an .xml file from your file manager straight onto the INPUT row to transform that file - exactly like picking a favorite: it becomes the input and opens as the active editor tab. The same green (loadable) / red (rejected) drag-over feedback applies, and the transform runs automatically as soon as both a stylesheet and an input are ready (while Run automatically is checked).

docs.title: Browsing favorites with ◀ / ▶
docs.text:
Pick stylesheets and input files straight from your Favorites and page through them, so you can run the same stylesheet over many files, or many stylesheets over one file, without ever opening a file chooser.

Both the STYLESHEET and the INPUT rows carry a star icon, a pair of ◀ / ▶ navigation buttons, and a small "i / n" position label. The ◀ / ▶ buttons and the label only appear once the browse list holds at least two entries.

  • The star menu lists the favorites of the matching type - XSLT favorites for STYLESHEET, XML favorites for INPUT - grouped by their folder (category). An "All … favorites" entry at the top selects the whole list at once.
  • Picking a favorite (or an "All"/folder entry) does three things: it sets the current file, it builds a browse list from that selection, and it loads the file into the editor. An input comes to the front as the active tab. A stylesheet opens behind the active tab while the input follows the active document (otherwise the stylesheet would become its own input); with a fixed input file it comes to the front too. The same happens on every ◀ / ▶ step.
  • The ◀ / ▶ buttons then step backward and forward through that browse list. Browsing is cyclic: pressing ▶ on the last entry wraps to the first, and ◀ on the first wraps to the last. The "i / n" label shows your position (for example, 3 / 12).
  • Each ◀ / ▶ step runs the transformation automatically (while Run automatically is checked) - but only once both sides are ready: a stylesheet is selected and an input is available (either a chosen input file or the active editor document). Until both are present, stepping just loads the file without transforming.

This supports two common workflows:

  1. Fix the input, step through stylesheets. Keep one XML file as input, then page through several data-quality or reporting stylesheets with ▶ to see each result in turn.
  2. Fix the stylesheet, step through inputs. Choose one XSLT stylesheet, then page through many XML input files with ▶ to apply the same transformation to each.

The existing Change file chooser, the clock (recent stylesheets) menu, and Use active editor all keep working exactly as before.

docs.title: OUTPUT METHOD
docs.text: A single dropdown with Auto, XML, HTML, XHTML, Text, JSON. Auto (the default) detects the output format from the stylesheet's xsl:output declaration; pick a concrete format to override the detection.

docs.title: PARAMETERS
docs.text:
Define XSLT parameters as name = value rows:

  • Add parameter adds a new row.
  • Each row has its own remove button.
  • The values are passed to the stylesheet on every run.

docs.title: Running a Transformation
docs.text:
1. Choose a stylesheet (STYLESHEET → Change, or pick one from the recent menu).
  2. Check the INPUT section shows the document you want to transform.
  3. Click Run Transform.

The Run automatically checkbox next to Run Transform (on by default) controls the automatic run that starts when you drop a stylesheet or input, pick one from your favorites, or browse with ◀ / ▶. Uncheck it to only set the file and run with Run Transform yourself.

The result appears in the OUTPUT panel below the editor - see The OUTPUT Panel below.

docs.title: Debugging a Stylesheet
docs.text:
Debug (next to Run Transform) runs the same stylesheet over the same input as Run Transform (the INPUT file when one is set by dropping, a favorite or ◀ / ▶ browsing, otherwise the active document) in the interactive XSLT debugger. The other ways in are Tools → Debug with XSLT…, the Transform ▾ → Debug with XSLT… toolbar entry, Run ▾ → Debug Transform for an active XSLT document (against the toolbar's Input target), the PDF / FOP panel's Debug stylesheet…, and Shift+F5 whenever a document is open.

What happens:

  1. The stylesheet opens as a document. The debugger runs its editor text - unsaved changes included, also of open included modules - under the file's location, so relative xsl:include / xsl:import hrefs resolve (a new stylesheet must be saved once). Every saved XSLT document already has a breakpoint gutter: click the slot left of a line to toggle a red breakpoint, before or during a session (the click does not move the caret). Breakpoints are remembered per file across sessions and restarts, including those set in included modules.
  2. The DEBUG dock opens below the editor, so the stylesheet stays visible while you step. The dock shares its space with OUTPUT; a small OUTPUT | DEBUG strip switches between them, and a result that arrives while DEBUG is in front marks the OUTPUT toggle.
  3. The run starts and pauses at the first instruction when there are no breakpoints (Pause on entry, a toggle in the dock's header), otherwise at the first breakpoint. The paused line is tinted in the editor and marked with a green arrow in the gutter (a yellow arrow on a breakpoint line). When Saxon pauses inside an included module, that file opens, with its own breakpoints in its gutter.

The dock's header holds the controls - Continue (F5), Pause (F6, breaks into a running transformation), Run to Cursor (Ctrl+F10; also gutter right-click → Run to Here, and it starts the debugger when none runs), Step Into (F7), Step Over (F8), Step Out (Shift+F8), Restart (runs again from the start with the same breakpoints, reading the stylesheet again from the editor), Stop, Pause on entry, Mute (all breakpoints off, steps still work), Show in editor, Show input (the paused context node in the input XML, which is tinted blue there), Evaluate (Alt+F8: any XPath in the selected frame, with a history on Up/Down) and ✕ (ends the session). Below it, two tab groups show the paused state - Variables | Watch on the left, Call Stack | Messages | Breakpoints | Output on the right, with a draggable divider whose position is remembered. Messages and Breakpoints carry a count badge; a failed run brings Messages to the front. The panels:

Panel Shows Variables The context item (.), position() / last(), the XSLT context (mode, current-group() / current-grouping-key(), regex-group(n), tunnel parameters, accumulator values), every local variable in scope and every global variable that has been evaluated so far - with real values and XDM types, as a tree: nodes unfold into attributes and children, sequences, maps and arrays into their items; each row's XPath can be watched. While paused, the stylesheet also shows each variable's value at the end of its declaration line (details), and resting the mouse on a $variable (or a selected XPath) shows its value in a popup. Click a value to open it in a window with the full, highlighted value, Copy, and an XPath field that runs against it (details) Watch Your XPath expressions, evaluated against the paused context item with the variables in scope (count(item), $total, position()); re-evaluated at every pause. Add / Remove sit above the table (or Variables → right-click → Add to Watches); Delete removes, F2 / double-click edits an expression; click a value to open the full result. Watches are saved per stylesheet Call Stack Template and function frames (instructions nested inside them are dimmed), each with its module and line; loops show their current item, e.g. ForEach (3 of 222); double-click jumps there, also into an include. Selecting a frame switches Variables and Watch to that frame (its context item, own locals and the globals). Enter / Open Value… opens the frame's context item, with XPath over that frame's own variables Messages xsl:message output and Saxon warnings as they happen, with their stylesheet location; double-click jumps to the line. Filter by level and text, Copy, Clear Breakpoints All breakpoints of the session, grouped by file (checkbox = enabled · file · line · condition · hit rule · hits of this run; after a completed run, breakpoints it never reached are flagged and drawn amber in the gutter) with Remove / Edit… / Template… (break whenever a template rule, named template, function or mode is entered, at any line) / Clear all / Break on ▾ (dynamic errors - pausing at the failing instruction with its variables -, terminating or all xsl:message) above the list (Delete removes the selected one); double-click jumps to the line; right-click an entry for per-file Enable / Disable / Remove and Export / Import Breakpoints…. Right-click a gutter slot for a conditional breakpoint (XPath, pauses only when true), a logpoint (writes item {@id}-style messages to Messages, optionally without pausing) or a hit count rule (exactly / from / every N-th hit) - details Output The output written so far, refreshed at every pause; the complete result once the run finishes. Secondary results (xsl:result-document, kept in memory) are selectable; Documents lists and opens what doc() / document() / collection() loaded

When the run ends, the status reads Finished · N ms and the result lands in the OUTPUT panel (the OUTPUT toggle lights up; DEBUG stays in front so the messages remain readable). A failed run shows the error with its location in Messages. The debugger runs on its own Saxon processor, so a normal Run Transform during a paused session is unaffected. Tools → Debug Configuration… saves per stylesheet the input (Run target or a file), parameters, output format and pause on entry; Re-run Last Debug (Ctrl+Shift+F5) repeats the last debug run with its input read again. Details and stylesheet tips: XSLT Developer → Interactive Live Debugger.

docs.title: Queries (XPath, XQuery, JSONPath)
docs.text: The Transform panel no longer has its own XPATH and XQUERY sections. Below the run controls, a short hint and an Open Query Console button take you to the Query Console, which runs XPath, XQuery and JSONPath queries against the open document and offers the saved queries (Snippets menu) and the XQuery Examples.

docs.title: OPTIONS & TOOLS
docs.text:
The collapsible OPTIONS & TOOLS section at the top of the panel (open by default - click its header to collapse it) holds everything secondary. First the run options, as checkboxes:

Option What it does Live preview Re-runs the transform automatically (debounced) while you edit the input document. Watch stylesheet file Re-runs the transform whenever the chosen stylesheet changes on disk - handy while editing the stylesheet in another tool. Profile run A transform also opens a read-only Profile tool tab (timings + per-template execution times). Trace run A transform also opens a Trace tool tab (template matches + xsl:message output). Auto-open result tab Additionally opens every successful result as a regular editor tab (HTML/XHTML results open rendered in the Preview view). Off by default.

Below the options, the advanced tools are labelled rows (icon + name):

Row What it does Debug XSLT… Same as the Debug button next to Run Transform: opens the stylesheet (with the breakpoints set in its gutter) and the DEBUG dock below the editor - see Debugging a Stylesheet. Batch Transform… Runs the chosen stylesheet - or, when no stylesheet is set, the active XQuery document - over many XML files, with per-file results and "Save All". Execution Statistics Opens the Execution Statistics tool tab (duration, CPU and memory per XSLT/XQuery/validation run). Runs are only recorded while Record execution statistics is enabled in the Settings page's DEVELOPER card.

XSLT version selection (1.0/2.0/3.0) is intentionally not offered: Saxon HE auto-detects the version from the stylesheet's version attribute, so an explicit selector would be cosmetic.

docs.title: The OUTPUT Panel (Results)
docs.text:
Transform and query results appear in an OUTPUT panel docked below the editor instead of opening editor tabs and a separate HTML-preview tool tab.

All Transform-panel results - XSLT transforms, XPath/JSONPath queries, and XQuery runs - appear in an OUTPUT panel that docks below the editor: the source document stays on top and the result shows underneath, while the Properties inspector keeps its full height. The panel persists across activity switches, so the last result stays visible while you work elsewhere.

The OUTPUT panel header shows:

  • A format badge (XML, HTML, …) for the result.
  • A status: a green check with Transformed · N ms · M chars on success (how long the run took and how large the output is), or a red error icon with the error message on failure.
  • View toggles - Preview | Text | Table:
    • Text - the result in a read-only code editor (the default): line numbers, syntax highlighting matching the result format (XML or JSON; plain text otherwise), and font zoom with Ctrl+mouse wheel (Ctrl+0 resets).
    • Preview - the result rendered as a web page; available for HTML/XHTML results only.
    • Table - available for XQuery results that return a sequence of items (auto-selected when applicable). Each item becomes a row, and the columns are taken from each item's child elements (or, if an item has no child elements, its attributes). A sequence of plain values is shown in a single value column.
  • Actions:
    • Open as Tab (Open result as editor tab) - opens the result as a regular document (Transform-Result.xml / .html / .json / .txt) that you can edit and save. An HTML/XHTML result opens as an HTML document rendered in the Preview view (switch to Text to see the markup); re-running the transform updates the open result tab, re-rendering the preview if it is showing.
    • Browser (Open in browser) - opens the result (typically HTML) in your system web browser.
    • Save… (Save result…) - writes the result straight to a file.
    • ✕ - hides the OUTPUT panel; it reappears automatically on the next run.

Note

In earlier versions, every transform opened a Transform-Result.* editor tab, and HTML output additionally opened an "HTML Preview" tool tab. Both were replaced by the OUTPUT panel: an editor tab now opens only via the panel's Open result as editor tab action or the Auto-open result tab option in OPTIONS & TOOLS, and HTML is rendered inline via the panel's Preview view.

docs.title: Unified Shell
docs.text: The application opens directly into the Unified Shell - one workspace that combines XML, XSD, XSLT, XProc, Schematron and JSON editing with all the validation, transformation, signing and documentation tools. The separate legacy tabs have been consolidated here.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Unified Shell is the single workspace for everything FreeXmlToolkit does. Instead of switching between separate editor pages, you open files as tabs in the central editor host and reach every tool through the activity bar on the left. You can work with an XML file next to its XSD schema, XSLT stylesheets and Schematron rules at the same time.

The Unified Shell: activity bar (left), Explorer side panel, editor host with an XML file (Text/Tree/Graphic view toggle), the Properties inspector (right) and the status bar.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Area Purpose Activity bar (far left) Switch tools / side panels: Explorer, Search, Favorites, Validation, Transform, Schema, Schema Library (its label wraps onto two lines), PDF/FOP, Signature, Settings - plus a FundsXML activity when the optional FundsXML extension is enabled (see FundsXML Panel). Always visible - it cannot be collapsed. (Settings, Schema Library and Signature open as a full page in the editor area - see Settings Page, Schema Library Page and Signature Page. Help is not an activity - it is the Help menu, see Help Menu & About.) Menu bar (very top) File / Edit / View / Tools / Help - every action of the toolbar, the Activity Bar and the keyboard shortcuts in one place (see Menu Bar). On macOS it is the system menu bar at the top of the screen. Header bar (top) The breadcrumb (application / active file), a centered search pill ("Run XPath / XQuery…", shortcut Ctrl+K) that opens the bottom Query Console when clicked, the ? button (opens the Help menu as a popup - same as F1) and the Theme button. Side panel The panel for the selected activity (e.g. the Transform panel, the Validation panel). Resizable and collapsible (see Resizing and collapsing the side panels). Editor host (center) Tabs of open documents, each with the Text, Tree and Graphic view modes - plus a rendered Preview for HTML documents (see View Modes). Inspector (right) View and edit the selected node's properties from any view. Resizable and collapsible (see Resizing and collapsing the side panels). Hidden automatically while a page without a document (Settings, Schema Library, Signature, reports, tool tabs) is selected. Status bar (bottom) Caret position (Ln/Col), character count, file type, the XSD / IntelliSense indicator, the encoding label (the charset the file was read in and is saved in, e.g. UTF-8 or ISO-8859-1), the last recorded run (Developer feature), a memory indicator and the active file's path (see Status Bar).

docs.title: Resizing and collapsing the side panels
docs.text:
Both the left side panel and the right Properties inspector can be resized and collapsed to give the editor more room - the activity bar always stays visible.

Resizing - the panels are not fixed-width:

  • Drag the thin divider line between a panel and the editor to make the panel wider or narrower (the mouse pointer turns into a horizontal resize arrow over the divider). Widen the panel when file names, validation messages, or property values get truncated.
  • Each panel keeps a minimum width of 200 px, and the editor in the middle always keeps at least 320 px - you cannot drag a panel so far that the editor disappears.
  • The chosen widths are remembered across restarts (per user).
  • When you resize the window, the panels keep their pixel width - only the editor column grows or shrinks (the same behavior as VS Code).

Collapsing - each panel can also be hidden completely:

  • Collapse: click the discreet collapse button at the panel's inner edge (a chevron pointing at a bar: |< on the left panel, >| on the inspector). The panel is hidden completely.
  • Re-open: click the matching toggle button in the editor toolbar (left-most toggle, a sidebar icon, for the side panel; right-most toggle, a mirrored sidebar icon, for the inspector) - the same mechanism on both sides. Selecting any activity from the activity bar also re-opens the left side panel. A re-opened panel comes back at its last dragged width.
  • The collapsed/expanded state is remembered across restarts and can also be changed under Settings → Appearance → LAYOUT ("Show left side panel" / "Show Properties (inspector) panel").
  • The inspector only appears next to documents. When you switch to a tab that is not a document - Settings, Schema Library, Signature, a report or another tool tab - the inspector hides automatically, so the page gets the full width. Its toggle button is greyed out on such tabs. As soon as you select a document tab again, the inspector comes back. Your own show/hide choice is not changed by this - if you had hidden the inspector, it stays hidden.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-tab editing - Open multiple files of different types in one view
  • Automatic file type detection - Files are recognized by extension (.xml/.wsdl, .xsd, .xsl/.xslt, .xpl/.xproc, .xq/.xquery/.xqm/.xqy, .xpath, .sch/.schematron, .json/.jsonc/.json5, .html/.htm/.xhtml); anything else opens as plain text
  • View modes per document - Text, Tree and Graphic, all over one shared model, plus a rendered Preview for HTML documents (see View Modes)
  • Inspector editing everywhere - edit node properties from the Text, Tree and Graphic views, not just one
  • Type picker with explanations - the inspector's Type field and Change Type… in the diagram and tree context menus list the schema's own types and every XSD built-in datatype, and a side pane explains the highlighted one (see Choosing a type)
  • Integrated XPath/XQuery - a bottom Query Console queries the active XML/JSON file right from the editor (Ctrl+Shift+X)
  • Editor toolbar actions - run Validate, Transform, Run, Generate Documentation and the Type Editor for the active document without switching activities
  • Search & Replace - Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H across the editor, in every view mode: the Text view searches the raw text, the Tree and Graphic views search the nodes themselves (names, documentation, attributes, enumeration and facet values, comments)
  • Find in Files & XPath search - the Search activity (Ctrl+Shift+F) searches and replaces across all files of a folder, by plain text or by XPath expression (see Search Panel)
  • Resizable side panels - drag the divider lines to give the side panel or the Properties inspector more room; the widths are remembered across restarts (see Resizing and collapsing the side panels)
  • Favorites - Quick access to frequently used files

docs.title: Colours: workflows and actions
docs.text:
Colour tells you two things at a glance, and the two never mix on one surface:

  • Which workflow you are in. Every activity has its own accent colour: Explorer brand blue, Search indigo, Favorites amber, Validation green, Transform orange, Schema purple, Schema Library grape, PDF / FOP rose, Signature cyan, FundsXML teal. The colour appears only on the chrome that names the workflow: the bar next to the selected Activity-Bar icon, the panel title (VALIDATION, TRANSFORM, …), the panel's one primary button (Run Validation, Run Transform, Generate PDF, Validate Signature), the tint of the matching toolbar group, the icons of the Welcome page's task list and the "last run" badge in the status bar. Settings stays neutral, so the default view of the app looks as before.
  • What an action does. Menu items and the action rows of the side panels colour their icon by the kind of action, in every editor and every view: green adds or creates (Add, Paste, Duplicate, Validate, Generate), red removes (Delete, Remove, Clear, Cut), orange edits in place (Rename, Edit value), cyan navigates to something that already exists (Go to Definition, Reveal, Find, opening a favorite or a generated PDF), purple changes structure (Change Type, Cardinality, Move Up/Down), blue runs a tool (Format, Sort, Save, Export, Download, "Open file…" with a file chooser) and grey is neutral (Copy, Expand/Collapse, Undo/Redo).

Result colours always win: a failed run shows a red icon on an orange Transform badge, a passed validation a green check. Both layers switch with the light/dark theme:

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. The Unified Shell opens automatically on startup.
  2. Use the Explorer activity (or File → Open) to open files; File → New (Ctrl+N) opens the guided New File dialog to create a new file from a template or schema. You can also drag & drop files from your file manager anywhere onto the window - every supported file type (XML, XSD, XSLT, XProc, XQuery, XPath, Schematron, JSON, HTML) opens as a new tab; other files are ignored.
  3. Files open as tabs in the editor host - switch tabs by clicking their headers (drag a header to reorder, right-click it for tab actions), and switch view modes (Text / Tree / Graphic - plus Preview for HTML files) with the segmented view switch.

After the first start, a small Anonymous usage statistics notice appears once in the bottom-right corner of the window. It explains that FreeXmlToolkit sends anonymous usage statistics and error reports (never file names, paths or content). Click OK to continue, Settings… to switch it off, or What is sent? to see the exact data. Nothing is sent before you have acknowledged this notice. See Privacy & Anonymous Telemetry.

docs.title: New File Dialog
docs.text:
Creating a new file opens a guided dialog instead of silently opening an empty, untitled document. You can pick a starting template or an XSD schema, so a new file already has a sensible structure.

The New File dialog opens whenever you create a new document - from the toolbar New button (Ctrl+N), the Explorer panel's New file action, or the New File card on the Welcome screen. It walks you through a few simple choices and then opens (and optionally saves) the new document.

Field What it does File type Choose XML, XSD, XSLT, Schematron, JSON, XProc, XQuery, XPath, or HTML. The rest of the dialog adapts to your choice. Template A list of available templates - the built-in library plus your own templates from Settings - automatically filtered to the selected file type. The default is "— None —" (start blank). Picking a parameterized template prompts you for its values when the file is created. Schema (plain XML only, and only when no template is chosen.) Pick an XSD to base the document on - from your Favorites, your Recent files, or Browse… to select a file. The chosen schema is also bound to the new document, so it appears in the Validation panel and drives IntelliSense. Pre-fill mandatory nodes (empty) (shown with the Schema option, on by default.) When a schema is selected, the new document is pre-populated with all required elements and attributes (left empty) generated from that schema, giving you a ready-to-fill skeleton. Save to (optional.) Choose a location with Browse… to write the file to disk immediately and open it. Leave it empty to open the document as an untitled tab - you will be asked for a location the first time you Save.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A template is rendered into the new document (prompting for any parameters first).
  • XML with a schema and "Pre-fill mandatory nodes" produces a skeleton containing every mandatory element and attribute from that schema.
  • Otherwise you get a minimal, valid starting point for the chosen type: an XML declaration for XML, an xs:schema skeleton for XSD, an xsl:stylesheet (version 3.0) skeleton for XSLT, an ISO-Schematron skeleton for Schematron, {} for JSON, a p:declare-step skeleton (with source/result ports and p:identity) for XProc, an xquery version "3.1"; prolog for XQuery, and a minimal HTML5 page skeleton for HTML.

docs.title: View Modes
docs.text:
The segmented view switch offers the Text, Tree, and Graphic view modes - each with its own icon - plus, for HTML documents only, a rendered read-only Preview (eye icon) - the Preview segment only appears while an HTML document is active. There is no separate Grid mode - the grid is part of Graphic.

Every document tab offers the same view modes:

Mode What it shows Text Source code editing with syntax highlighting Tree The document as a hierarchical tree Graphic A visual editor that depends on the document type: for XML, XSLT, Schematron and JSON files it shows the editable XMLSpy-style grid; for XSD files it shows the schema diagram Preview (HTML documents only.) The page rendered read-only in an embedded web view - see HTML Preview

All views share one in-memory model per document, so edits and Undo/Redo history are preserved when you switch views.

docs.title: The Grid (Graphic view for XML)
docs.text: The Graphic view of XML and JSON documents is an editable grid with tables for repeating elements, opened cells, entry helpers, filters and formulas - see Grid View.

docs.title: HTML Preview (Preview view for HTML)
docs.text:
HTML documents (.html, .htm, .xhtml) get their own Preview view mode - the eye icon in the segmented view switch - that renders the page read-only, the way a browser would show it:

  • HTML files open in Preview by default. Whether you open them from the Explorer, by drag & drop, or via the Open dialog, you see the rendered page first.
  • Editing happens in the Text view. Switch to Text to change the markup, then switch back to Preview - it re-renders your current editor text, including unsaved changes.
  • Tree and Graphic are disabled for HTML documents, because HTML output is often not well-formed XML.
  • Transform results render here too. The OUTPUT panel's Open result as editor tab opens an HTML/XHTML transform result as an HTML document showing its Preview, and re-running the transform updates the open result tab live - see The OUTPUT Panel.

Preview limitations

  • The page is rendered without a base URL, so relative references - external CSS files, images - do not resolve. Inline styles render fine. To view a transform result together with its external assets, use the OUTPUT panel's Open in browser action instead.
  • Ctrl+F in the Preview searches the document's underlying markup text, not the rendered page.
  • The Preview is read-only - all editing happens in the Text view.

docs.title: Every Picked File Opens in the Editor
docs.text:
Whichever way you pick a file, it is loaded into the editor as a tab (an open tab is reused): File → Open… and Open Recent, the Welcome page's recent list, the Explorer and Favorites panels, drag & drop onto the window or onto a panel row, and on every page the Change / Choose… dialogs, the recent menus (Transform clock icon, Explorer Transform with Other Stylesheet / Validate with Other Schematron) and the favorites star menus.

  • An input (Transform or PDF/FOP XML input) becomes the active tab.
  • A stylesheet opens behind the active tab while the input follows the active document, and in front when the input is a fixed file.
  • A schema, Schematron, JSON Schema, catalog or query target opens behind the active tab, so the document it applies to stays in front.
  • On a page in the main area (Signature, Schema Library) the file opens behind the page.

Not loaded: keystores and trust stores (binary files), and spreadsheets for import (the converted XML opens instead).

docs.title: Working with Editor Tabs
docs.text:
• Reorder tabs by dragging a tab header left or right. The Explorer's OPEN EDITORS list follows the new order.
  • Right-click a tab for a menu that acts on that tab, even if it is not the active one:
Menu item What it does Reload from Disk Reads the file again. If the document has unsaved changes, you are asked first. Not available for untitled documents. Close Closes the tab (asks to save unsaved changes). Close Others Closes every other tab. Each tab with unsaved changes still asks to save; Cancel stops closing the rest. Save / Save As… Saves the document. For an untitled document, Save works like Save As…. Copy Path Copies the file's full path to the clipboard. Reveal in File Manager Shows the file in Windows Explorer, the macOS Finder or your Linux file manager, with the file selected (if the file manager cannot select it, its folder opens). Reveal in Explorer Panel Opens the Explorer and selects the file in the workspace tree. If the file lies outside the current workspace, its folder becomes the workspace.

Copy Path and the two Reveal items need a saved file, so they are disabled for untitled documents. Tabs that show no document - tool tabs such as the Type Editor, a diff or a PDF preview - only offer Close and Close Others.

docs.title: Files Changed Outside the Editor
docs.text:
The shell watches the files of all open tabs. When another program changes or deletes one of them, a dialog asks what to do - checked every two seconds while the FreeXmlToolkit window is active, and immediately when you switch back to it.

Situation Choice Result File changed on disk Reload The tab shows the file's new content. Unsaved changes in that tab are discarded (the dialog warns you when there are any). Caret position and view mode (Text / Tree / Graphic) are kept. Ignore The tab keeps its content and is marked as unsaved (●), because it now differs from the file. Saving overwrites the external change. You are not asked again until the file changes once more. File deleted on disk Keep The tab stays open and is marked as unsaved (●). Save creates the file again. Close The tab is closed, including any unsaved changes.

Closing the dialog with Esc counts as Ignore / Keep. With several affected files the dialogs appear one after the other, each with its tab brought to the front.

Note

  • Saving from the editor itself never triggers the dialog, and neither does a file that was merely touched or rewritten with identical content.
  • Changing a tab's file from elsewhere in the application - for example saving the right side of a diff, or exporting a result over a file that is open - is reported like any other outside change.
  • Untitled documents are not watched.

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text: Type Extensions Features XML .xml, .wsdl Text + graphic view, XSD/Schematron linking, IntelliSense, continuous validation XSD .xsd Text + graphic view, Type Library, Type Editor, Schema Analysis, Documentation, Sample Data, Flatten XSLT .xsl, .xslt XSLT editor + XML input + output preview, live transform, parameters, performance metrics XProc .xpl, .xproc Pipeline editor (Text + Tree view), Run Pipeline via the embedded XML Calabash engine - see XProc Pipelines XQuery .xq, .xquery, .xqm, .xqy Query editor with highlighting + IntelliSense, Run Query against a selectable target - see Query Documents XPath .xpath Single-expression query editor, Run Query against a selectable target - see Query Documents Schematron .sch, .schematron Code editor + Visual Builder + Tester + Documentation Generator JSON .json, .jsonc, .json5 Text + tree + editable grid view (see The Grid for JSON), JSONPath queries, JSON Schema validation. The JSON/JSONC/JSON5 flavor is detected from the content, so comments and trailing commas are accepted in any of the three. HTML .html, .htm, .xhtml Rendered read-only Preview (the default view) + Text editing; also the format of HTML/XHTML transform results opened as editor tabs - see HTML Preview

docs.title: Menu Bar
docs.text:
The menu bar offers every shell action by name, with its keyboard shortcut next to it. Items that do not apply to the active document are greyed out (e.g. Type Editor is only available for XSD schemas, Save needs an open document).

Menu Contents File New…, Open…, Open from URL…, Open Recent (the last opened files), Close Tab, Save, Save As…, Save All, Settings…, Exit (Ctrl+Q; asks to save unsaved changes first) Edit Undo, Redo, Find…, Replace…, Find in Files…, Replace in Files…, Format Document, Minify, Insert Template… View The view modes (Text / Tree / Graphic / Preview), Side Panel, Properties Inspector, Query Console, Favorites Panel, Activities (jump to any activity), Show Constraints in Diagram, Toggle Light / Dark Theme, Full Screen Tools Validate, Run, Transform with XSLT…, Debug with XSLT… (Shift+F5), Debug Configuration…, Re-run Last Debug (Ctrl+Shift+F5), Toggle Breakpoint (F9), Run to Cursor (Ctrl+F10), Set Schema…, Generate Documentation…, Generate Sample XML…, Generate XSD from XML, Generate XSD from XML Files…, Type Editor, Compare with File…, Spreadsheet Converter…, Add to Favorites Help Documentation, Keyboard Shortcuts, FundsXML Website and FundsXML Schema Docs (only while the FundsXML extension is enabled), Report a Problem… (when error reporting is enabled), GitHub Repository, Sponsor this Project, Check for Updates…, About FreeXmlToolkit - see Help Menu & About

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
On macOS the menus appear in the system menu bar and follow the platform conventions:

  • The FreeXmlToolkit application menu holds About FreeXmlToolkit, Check for Updates…, Settings… (Cmd+,), Hide FreeXmlToolkit (Cmd+H), Hide Others, Show All and Quit FreeXmlToolkit (Cmd+Q). These items are therefore not repeated in File and Help.
  • A Window menu offers Minimize, Zoom and Bring All to Front.
  • All shortcuts use Cmd instead of Ctrl. Because Cmd+H hides the application, Find and Replace is Alt+Cmd+F on macOS; full screen is Ctrl+Cmd+F (F11 works too).

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
The editor toolbar is a single slim row. Related actions sit in split buttons with a visible ▾ arrow menu: Save As / Save All live under Save ▾, Minify under Format ▾, Run Query / Run Transform / Run Pipeline under Run ▾, and Set XSD Schema… / Generate Documentation… / Type Editor… under Schema ▾.

The toolbar shows only what you can use right now. Without a document - on the Welcome page, or while a page such as Settings, Signature or Schema Library is in front - it shows just New and Open; the document groups (Save, Undo/Redo, Format, Query Console, Transform, Run, Schema, Validate) and the Text / Tree / Graphic view switch are hidden rather than shown greyed out. They come back as soon as a document tab is active.

There is no hidden "overflow" menu. Less frequent tools - Insert Template… (Ctrl+T), Compare with File… and Spreadsheet Converter… (Ctrl+E) - are in the Menu Bar (Edit and Tools menus) instead of the toolbar; their shortcuts work as before. Only when the window gets very narrow does the row wrap onto a second line as a fallback. The toolbar groups its actions three ways:

docs.title: Labeled buttons (frequent actions)
docs.text:
• New (Ctrl+N) - Open the guided New File dialog to create an XML, XSD, XSLT, Schematron, JSON, XProc, XQuery, XPath, or HTML file from a template or schema
  • Open (Ctrl+O) - Open one or more files
  • Validate (F8) - Validate the active document; this is the toolbar's primary action and the only filled button in the row - it is filled in the green of the Validation workflow (see Colours: workflows and actions). XML validates against the bound XSD/Schematron if one is set, otherwise for well-formedness.

docs.title: Split buttons (click the ▾ arrow for related actions)
docs.text:
Clicking the button itself runs the main action; clicking the small ▾ arrow opens a menu with the closely related actions:

Split button Primary click Arrow (▾) menu Save Save the current tab (Ctrl+S) Save As… (Ctrl+Shift+S) - save under a new name (the file chooser is pre-set to the tab's file type) · Save All - save every open tab at once Format Pretty-print the active document (Shift+Alt+F; note: Ctrl+Shift+F opens the Search panel, not document search). XML is indented by two spaces per level and every start tag stays on one line, however many attributes it carries Minify - remove all insignificant whitespace Run Run the active document against the selected Input (Ctrl+Enter) - the primary click automatically runs whichever action the active file type supports Run Query (XPath/XQuery) · Run Transform (XSLT) · Debug Transform (XSLT, Shift+F5 - the active stylesheet in the debugger) · Debug Query (XQuery, Shift+F5 - the same debugger on a query) · Debug Schematron (Schematron, Shift+F5 - the debugger on the Schematron's checks, against the selected Input; the primary click on a Schematron tab) · Run Pipeline (XProc) Transform Transform with XSLT… - opens the Transform panel on the active XML document, asks for a stylesheet if none is set, and runs it there (result in the OUTPUT panel) Transform with XSLT… · Debug with XSLT… (Shift+F5) - the same, but in the debugger Schema Set XSD Schema… - bind an XSD to the active document for IntelliSense and validation Set XSD Schema… · Generate Documentation… (HTML/PDF/Word for the active XSD) · Type Editor… (edit a named type of the active XSD) · Generate XSD from XML (infer a schema from the active XML document) · Generate XSD from XML Files… (infer one schema from several XML files)
  • Transform is a split button, see above: the primary click transforms, the ▾ arrow offers Debug with XSLT…

docs.title: Icon-only buttons (hover for the tooltip)
docs.text:
• Undo (Ctrl+Z) / Redo (Ctrl+Y)
  • Query Console - Shows / hides the bottom XPath/XQuery console (terminal icon). Ctrl+Shift+X shows or hides it; Ctrl+K (and the header's Run XPath / XQuery… pill) opens it and puts the cursor in the query.

docs.title: Type-gating and the Input dropdown
docs.text: The document actions act on the active document and are enabled only when they apply to its type (greyed out otherwise) - this covers Validate, Transform with XSLT…, the Run button and its menu entries (and Tools → Run / F5), and the Schema menu's Generate Documentation… / Type Editor… / Generate Sample XML… (also in Tools). The Input dropdown (labelled "Input: …", formerly Target) appears next to Run only while a query, XSLT, or XProc document is active and selects the XML document the run works on. See Editor Toolbar Document Actions and Query Documents & the Input Selector below.

docs.title: Panel Toggles
docs.text:
• Side panel (Ctrl+L) - Show/hide the left side panel (the active activity's Explorer, Validation, Transform, Schema, … panel); the same as the collapse button (|<) at the panel's inner edge
  • Query Console (Ctrl+Shift+X) - Show/hide the bottom XPath/XQuery query console (terminal icon in the editor toolbar). See Query Console below.
  • Properties (Ctrl+Shift+P) - Show/hide properties and validation sidebar. For XML files, the properties inspector lets you view and edit a node's properties (element name, namespace, attributes, and text content) from all three views - Text, Tree, and Graphic (the grid). For XSD files, the same inspector lets you edit a schema node's properties from all three XSD views - Text, Tree, and Graphic. See Properties Inspector below.
  • Favorites (Ctrl+Shift+D) - Show/hide the favorites panel (Ctrl+D adds the active document to favorites)

docs.title: XSD Views & Tools
docs.text:
When editing an XSD file, the editor host and the Schema activity provide:

An XSD open in the Graphic view, with the Schema activity panel (Type Library, Flatten, Schema Analysis, Generate Sample XML / Documentation) on the left.

The same schema in the Tree view - select a node to edit its properties in the inspector.

  • Text - Source code editing with syntax highlighting; moving the caret into a schema construct also lets you edit its properties in the Properties pane (see Properties Inspector)
  • Graphic - Visual schema diagram of cards (name, type, cardinality - see Reading a Card); drag cards to move nodes, hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) to copy (see Moving and Copying by Drag and Drop)
  • Type Editor - Edit ComplexTypes graphically, SimpleTypes with form editor
  • Analysis - The Schema Analysis tool tab: statistics incl. complexity metrics, unused types / groups and circular references, a Types tab with usage locations and "Remove unused", quality checks with score, identity constraints, XPath validation - every finding reveals its node in the Tree view, and the whole report exports as CSV / JSON / HTML / PDF / Excel (see Schema Analysis)
  • Documentation - Generate HTML/Word/PDF documentation (see below)
  • Sample Data - Generate sample XML from the schema
  • Flatten - Merge included schemas into a single standalone file. The Flatten Schema… button opens an options dialog first: strip annotations, strip XML comments, remove unused global types and groups, and minify the output — all checked by default for a minimal schema suited to server-side validation; uncheck everything for a plain flatten that keeps documentation. Imports (xs:import, different namespaces) are never merged. See XSD Flattener for details.

Missing imported schemas resolve automatically

If a schema's xs:import points to a file that is not found next to the schema, the toolkit looks it up in the Schema Library and your XML catalogs, then in the schema cache, and finally downloads it from the declared or namespace URL into the cache - so the imported types still appear in the Tree and Graphic views, even offline on later loads. Nested imports inside imported schemas are followed too, and your own schema files are never modified. See Automatic Resolution of Imported Schemas.

docs.title: The Schema Panel
docs.text:
The Schema activity's side panel lists the active schema's top-level declarations, grouped into GLOBAL ELEMENTS, COMPLEX TYPES, and SIMPLE TYPES (collapsible sections), with a filter field above them. Click a declaration to reveal it in the Tree view; double-click a type to open it in its dedicated Type Editor tab; right-click for Reveal in Tree / Open Type Editor / Find Usage. The + button in the COMPLEX TYPES and SIMPLE TYPES headers declares a new type and opens it in its Type Editor (see Creating a New Type). The schema tools (Generate Sample XML…, Sample XML with Options…, Flatten Schema…, Schema Analysis, Generate Documentation…) are labelled rows in the TOOLS section at the top of the panel - each row shows an icon and the tool's name, so nothing hides behind a tooltip. TOOLS starts open; click its header to collapse it.

Generate XSD from XML (infer a schema from the active XML document) and Generate XSD from XML Files… (infer one schema from several XML files) are not in the Schema panel - they are in the editor toolbar's Schema ▾ split menu.

The whole panel is a drop zone: drop an .xsd file from your file manager anywhere on it to open that schema as a document - the panel then shows its declarations. Unlike the picker drop targets elsewhere in the shell, this drop opens the file rather than binding or selecting anything. While dragging, the panel shows a dashed green border with a soft tint for an .xsd file and a dashed red border for any other extension - a red drop is rejected and does not open the file.

docs.title: Documentation Generator (editor area)
docs.text:
Generate Documentation… (Schema panel TOOLS section or the editor toolbar's Schema ▾ menu) opens the generator as a tab in the main editor area with the full option set:

  • SOURCE & OUTPUT - the XSD (the active schema is pre-filled) and the output folder (HTML) or file (PDF/Word).
  • FORMAT - HTML, PDF, or Word.
  • OPTIONS - Markdown rendering (All documentation, Per node (@markdown), or Off), type definitions in source code, documentation in diagrams, SVG overview page, metadata, the diagram image format (SVG/PNG/JPG), and a favicon (.ico/.png/.svg) embedded into the generated HTML site. See Generation Options for what the Markdown settings do.
  • PDF/WORD OPTIONS (shown for those formats) - page size (A4/Letter/Legal, PDF also A3), orientation, and the content building blocks (cover page, table of contents, data dictionary, schema/element diagrams). PDF additionally offers the color scheme (Blue/Green/Purple/Grayscale/Professional), a watermark (Draft/Confidential/Internal Use Only), page numbers, and PDF bookmarks.
  • LANGUAGES - Scan languages discovers the xml:lang documentation languages in the schema; pick which to include and the fallback language.
  • PROGRESS - the right-hand log streams the pipeline's task messages live while generating; the run can be cancelled, and the result can open automatically.

docs.title: XSLT Features
docs.text:
XSLT work happens in the Transform Panel (Activity Bar → Transform):

  • Run Transform - Run an XSLT transformation against the chosen input
  • Live preview (OPTIONS & TOOLS section) - Re-run automatically while you edit
  • Parameters - Define XSLT parameters (name = value rows)
  • Output method - Auto-detect or choose XML, HTML, XHTML, Text, or JSON output
  • Timing - The OUTPUT panel status shows execution time and output size
  • Debug (next to Run Transform, also Tools → Debug with XSLT… / Shift+F5) - the interactive debugger: breakpoints, stepping, variables, call stack, watches and live xsl:message output in a DEBUG dock below the stylesheet - see Debugging a Stylesheet
  • Profile / Trace (OPTIONS & TOOLS section) - Per-template timings and the template-match trace with xsl:message output of a normal run
  • Open in browser - View HTML output in your default browser from the OUTPUT panel

docs.title: XProc Pipelines
docs.text: .xpl / .xproc documents run with the embedded XML Calabash 3 engine - see XProc Pipelines.

docs.title: Transform Panel
docs.text: The Transform activity runs XSLT transformations: stylesheet, input, output method, parameters, live transform, debugging and the OUTPUT panel - see Transform Panel.

docs.title: Explorer Panel
docs.text:
Open the Explorer panel from the activity bar to manage files.

  • Header actions (top right): New file, Open folder, Refresh workspace. New file opens the same guided New File dialog as the toolbar's New button. The sections appear from top to bottom in this order:

  • OPEN EDITORS - one row per open document. The active document is highlighted (blue, bold) and unsaved documents show a dot on the right. Click a row to switch to that document. The list shows about six rows; with more open documents it scrolls, so the workspace tree below keeps its space. The rows follow the order of the editor tabs - drag a tab to reorder both.

  • Workspace - the file tree of the opened folder; the section is titled after the folder's name. Folders expand with their chevron; double-click (or Enter) opens a file. Only XML-family and JSON files are shown. While no folder is open, the section shows a short hint ("No folder open. Open a folder to browse its XML, XSD and stylesheet files here.") and an Open folder… button.

  • TOOLS - a collapsible section above the files with the file tools. It is open by default; whether you leave it open or closed is remembered. Transforming and Schematron-validating the selected files is done from the workspace tree's context menu; the tools of the other workflows (validate, transform, schema documentation, …) live in their own activities.

    Row What it does Open file… Opens a file with a file chooser. Open from URL… Opens a file from a web address (same as File → Open from URL…). Compare files… With two files selected in the workspace tree: compares them side by side. With one file selected: asks for a second file and compares the two. With no selection: compares the active document with a file you pick (same as Tools → Compare with File…). Disabled while there is neither a selection nor an open document. Spreadsheet Converter… Converts between XML and Excel / CSV (same as Tools → Spreadsheet Converter…, Ctrl+E). Generate XSD from XML files… Infers one schema from the XML files selected in the workspace tree and opens it as a new tab; with no XML file selected, asks you to pick the files (same as Tools → Generate XSD from XML Files…). Clear recent Empties the RECENT list.

  • RECENT - at the bottom, the recently opened files; click one to reopen it (drag the thin grip above the list to change its height). Favorites are not listed here: manage them in the Favorites activity (View → Favorites Panel, Ctrl+Shift+D) and use them via the star menus; Ctrl+D adds the active document to your favorites.

  • Collapsible sections - the OPEN EDITORS, workspace and TOOLS section headers are clickable: click a header to collapse or expand its section (the chevron next to the title flips accordingly). Use this to give the file tree more room when you have many open editors.

Binding an XSD

The Explorer has no XSD picker. Bind a schema to the active document via the status-bar schema indicator, Tools → Set Schema… / the toolbar's Schema ▾ button, or the Validation panel's SOURCES section.

docs.title: Transform and Validate from the Explorer
docs.text:
Run an XSLT stylesheet or a Schematron against XML files straight from the Explorer, without switching to the Transform or Validation activity first.

Select one or more XML files in the workspace tree (hold Ctrl or Shift while clicking to select several), then right-click them. The context menu offers:

Entry What it does Open Opens the selected file(s) in the editor. Transform with <stylesheet> Transforms the selection with the last-used stylesheet (the entry names it). Reads Transform with XSLT… while no stylesheet has been used yet - you are then asked to pick one. Transform with Other Stylesheet ▸ Lists your recently used stylesheets and Choose stylesheet…; picking one makes it the current stylesheet and runs the transform. Validate with <Schematron> Validates the selection with the last-used Schematron (the entry names it). Reads Validate with Schematron… while none has been used yet - you are then asked to pick one. Validate with Other Schematron ▸ Lists your recently used Schematrons, your Schematron Favorites, Choose Schematron… and Clear recent. Compare Selected Files Compares the two selected files side by side (enabled with exactly two files selected). Generate XSD from Selected Infers one schema from the selected XML files and opens it as a new tab.

When nothing is selected in the tree, Transform and Validate use the active editor document (if it is XML).

The last-used stylesheet and Schematron are sticky and shared with the Transform panel and the Validation panel: both places draw from the same recent lists.

What Transform does depends on how many XML files are selected:

  • One XML file (or the active document): the stylesheet runs and the result appears in the docked Transform OUTPUT panel below the editor. HTML dashboards render in the Preview (WebView). The output format is auto-detected from the stylesheet's xsl:output declaration.
  • Several XML files: the Batch Transform tool tab opens, pre-loaded with those files, and the run starts automatically. Save the results with Save All….

What Validate does: the chosen Schematron is also bound to the active document, so the Validation panel and live validation use it too. The result is shown in the Validation activity: a single document runs through the normal single-file flow (problems list, detailed Schematron report), a multi-file selection through the batch flow with one RESULTS row per file. Batch runs additionally check each file against the active document's bound XSD (if any) - bind or clear the XSD in the Validation panel's SOURCES section to control that.

Tip

Primary workflow: choose your stylesheet once, then just select another XML file in the tree and right-click Transform with <stylesheet> again - the stylesheet stays put. For output-format overrides, parameters, watch-and-rerun, and the result table, use the full Transform panel.

docs.title: Search Panel
docs.text:
A dedicated Search activity brings VS-Code-style Find in Files with Replace, plus an XPath search & replace that works across whole folders. Heads-up: its shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+F - formatting lives on Shift+Alt+F (see Keyboard Shortcuts).

Open the Search panel from the magnifying-glass icon in the activity bar (directly below Explorer), or press Ctrl+Shift+F - any text selected in the editor is prefilled as the search term - or Ctrl+Shift+H, which opens the same panel with the replace row already expanded. A Find text | Find by XPath toggle at the top switches between the panel's two modes.

docs.title: Find text (Find in Files)
docs.text:
Searches all files of a folder for plain text. Results appear as you type - the search re-runs automatically after a short pause.

  • Where it searches - the Search in folder line shows the folder's name (hover for the full path, or "No folder — choose one" when none is set). By default it is the folder opened in the Explorer workspace (falling back to the last-used directory); the Browse button picks any other folder. The Files matching field filters which files are searched - it defaults to the XML-family extensions (*.xml,*.xsd,*.xsl,*.xslt,*.sch,*.schematron,*.json,*.xq,*.xquery,*.xqm,*.xqy,*.xpath,*.xpl,*.xproc).
  • Options - labelled switches below the search field: Match case, Whole word, Regex (regular expression) and Replace (shows the replace row).
  • Results - before the first search, the result area shows a short hint on what to type. Matches are grouped file → matches in a tree with checkboxes. Click a match to open the file and select the exact match in the Text view. All matches in the active document are also highlighted in the editor (translucent amber).
  • Limits - files larger than 20 MB and binary files are skipped, and at most 1000 matches are listed per file (the file then shows a "More matches not shown" note). Open documents with unsaved changes are searched via their live editor content, so what you see in the editor is what is found.

docs.title: Replace in Files
docs.text:
Click the Replace switch (or open the panel with Ctrl+Shift+H) to reveal the replace row:

  1. Type the replacement text. In regular-expression mode, $1-style group references in the replacement insert the matched groups.
  2. Untick any matches you want to keep - only the checked matches are replaced.
  3. Click Replace… and confirm the summary dialog.

Replacements are applied safely:

  • Open documents are edited in the editor, as exactly one undo step per document - press Ctrl+Z to revert everything at once, then save normally.
  • Files not open in the editor are written to disk atomically, preserving their encoding (BOM, ISO-8859-1, …) and line endings.
  • A file that changed on disk after the search ran is skipped and reported - it is never overwritten with stale results. Re-run the search and replace again.

docs.title: Find by XPath
docs.text:
Find & replace by XPath in a document or across a folder. For queries against the open document, use the Query Console (Ctrl+K).

Evaluates an XPath 3.1 expression (Saxon; the map, array, math, fn and xs prefixes are pre-declared) and lists the matching nodes:

  • Scope - a Document | Folder toggle: evaluate against the active document, or against every file of a folder (with its own file-glob filter, default *.xml). The folder line shows the folder's name (full path as tooltip), or "No folder — choose one" when none is set. Before the first search, the result area shows a short hint.
  • Namespaces - enter bindings as prefix=uri lines (an empty prefix sets the default element namespace). The Detect button reads the bindings from the active document's root element, so you rarely have to type them.
  • Find matches lists the matched elements, attributes and text nodes with line numbers and a short preview. Click a result to navigate to the exact node; matches are highlighted in the editor. Nodes that cannot be mapped to a text position (comments, processing instructions) are excluded and reported as a count.

docs.title: Replacing via XPath
docs.text:
Pick a Replace mode, then click Replace checked… and confirm - as in Find text mode, only the checked matches are changed:

Mode What it does Set value Sets the matched element's text (or the matched attribute's value) to a literal you type. Compute value (XPath) Computes the new value per match, with the matched node as the context - for example concat(., '-suffix') or string(number(.) * 2). Delete nodes Removes the matched nodes: elements (including the whole line when the element sits alone on it), attributes (with the surrounding whitespace), or text. Replace with XML Replaces matched elements with an XML fragment you enter. The fragment is checked for well-formedness, and multi-line fragments are re-indented to fit their new location.

All XPath replacements are formatting-preserving text edits - outside the replaced ranges the document stays byte-for-byte identical. In the active document the whole replacement is one undo step (Ctrl+Z reverts it). In folder mode, open files are edited via the editor and all other files are written to disk atomically, with the same changed-on-disk staleness check as Find text mode.

docs.title: Favorites Panel
docs.text:
Open the Favorites panel from the star icon in the activity bar for one-click access to your saved files.

  • Favorites are grouped by their folder as soon as you use folders (the rest gathers under Uncategorized); without folders they group by file type. Every entry shows a colored type icon.
  • The search field filters the list by name or path as you type.
  • Click a favorite to open it as an editor tab. Right-click for Open, Rename…, Move to folder (existing folders, (No folder), or New folder…), and Remove.
  • The action rows at the top: Add current stars the active document, Manage… opens the management view described below.

docs.title: Manage Favorites (editor area)
docs.text:
Click Manage… to open the full management view as a tab in the main editor area:

  • A FOLDERS list on the left filters the table (All, the smart collections, Uncategorized, your folders) and offers New…, Rename…, and Delete (deleting a folder moves its favorites to Uncategorized - nothing is lost).
  • Smart collections: Recently Used (favorites you actually opened, latest first) and Most Popular (most-opened first) - opening a favorite anywhere in the app feeds them automatically.
